title: Dust
description: Small particles in the air and settling onto surfaces
wiki_lead:
Dust is made of fine particles of solid matter. On Earth, it generally consists of particles in the atmosphere that come from various sources such as soil lifted by wind (an aeolian process), volcanic eruptions, and pollution. Dust can be considered an aerosol when fine particles remain suspended in the atmosphere for extended time.
Dust in homes, offices, and other built environments is composed of about 20–50% dead skin cells. The rest, is composed of small amounts of plant pollen, human hairs, animal fur, textile fibers, paper fibers, minerals from outdoor soil, burnt meteorite particles, and many other materials which may be found in the local environment.
Total suspended dust (TSD) concentration, as measured in mg/m3, can vary between 0.01 to 10,000 mg/m3 in various outdoor environments: residential, industrial, and commercial areas, highways, dirt roads (single or multiple vehicle traffic), quarries, and sand storms.

Dust is made of fine particles of solid matter. On Earth, it generally consists of particles in the atmosphere that come from various sources such as soil lifted by wind (an aeolian process), volcanic eruptions, and pollution. Dust can be considered an aerosol when fine particles remain suspended in the atmosphere for extended time.
Dust in homes, offices, and other built environments is composed of about 20–50% dead skin cells. The rest, is composed of small amounts of plant pollen, human hairs, animal fur, textile fibers, paper fibers, minerals from outdoor soil, burnt meteorite particles, and many other materials which may be found in the local environment.
Total suspended dust (TSD) concentration, as measured in mg/m3, can vary between 0.01 to 10,000 mg/m3 in various outdoor environments: residential, industrial, and commercial areas, highways, dirt roads (single or multiple vehicle traffic), quarries, and sand storms.


Atmospheric

Atmospheric or wind-borne fugitive dust, also known as aeolian process dust, as transported through the troposphere, primarily comes from saltation and dry regions where high-speed winds can remove mostly silt-sized, up to 1/16mm, material that will abrade susceptible surfaces to create more dust. This includes areas where grazing, ploughing, vehicle use, and other human behaviors have further destabilized the land, though not all dust source areas have been largely affected by anthropogenic impacts. Dust-producing surfaces cover one-third of the global land area, roughly 13 billion hectares, made up of hyper-arid regions like the Sahara, which covers 0.9 billion hectares, and drylands, which occupy 5.2 billion hectares.
Airborne dust is considered an aerosol that once in the atmosphere can produce strong local radiative forcing and intensity can be measured by the aerosol optical depth(AOD). Saharan dust, in particular, can be transported and deposited as far as the Caribbean and the Amazon basin and may affect air temperature, ocean temperature, and rainfall amounts.


Middle East
Dust in the Middle East has been a historic phenomenon. Recently, because of climate change and the escalating process of desertification, aerosol optical depth in the Middle East has been increasing. As a multi-factor phenomenon, there is not yet a clear consensus on the sources or potential solutions to adjust Middle Eastern dust levels.


Iran
Dust in Iraq and Iran are migratory systems that move from west to east and have the highest intensity, concentration, and extent until mid-summer, then reverse and flow from east to west in the spring.  The causes of their occurrence are the lack of humidity, dry environment, low rainfall, and annual droughts. Due to the decrease of rainfall in areas such as Iraq and Syria, most of the dust in Iran also originates from the regions of Iraq, Syria, and Jordan.
In Iran, foreign dust contributions have formed new dust areas in recent years or increased the size of existing dust areas. Among these areas, parts of southern Tehran, south of Alborz province – which in the past were plains, riverbeds, seasonal lakes, and seasonal reservoirs – and Gavkhoni wetland of Isfahan province have become dry and prone to dust. 
Qom salt lake in Qom province, Hamun lake, and Urmia lake areas have become dust centers, due to strong winds, and lake size reduction, primarily due to drought,, where some areas of the lake which were previously underwater are now exposed to wind erosion.
In Iran, the dust directly affects more than 5 million people and has become a serious government issue recently.[1] In the Khuzestan province, it has led to the severe increase of air pollution. The amount of pollutants in the air has surpassed more than 50 times the normal level several times in a year.

grok_lead: Dust consists of fine solid particles, typically ranging from submicrometer to several hundred micrometers in diameter, that are dispersed in the air or deposited on surfaces, arising from mechanical breakdown of materials such as soil, rock fragments, organic debris, and anthropogenic emissions. Atmospheric dust originates predominantly from wind erosion of arid and semi-arid soils, contributing about 70% of airborne particles, with lesser inputs from volcanic activity, industrial processes, and biomass burning, influencing global climate through scattering and absorption of solar radiation as well as ocean fertilization via iron-rich deposits. In household settings, dust accumulates as a mixture of desquamated human and pet skin cells, textile fibers, tracked-in outdoor particles, and microbial elements like dust mites and fungal spores, often enriched with trace metals and organic pollutants that can trigger respiratory issues and allergies upon repeated exposure. Fine dust fractions, particularly those below 2.5 micrometers (PM2.5), penetrate deep into lungs and enter bloodstreams, correlating with elevated risks of cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases based on epidemiological data, though natural dust events like Saharan plumes also deposit essential minerals benefiting distant ecosystems.
